purpose: Correct two demonstrated display-oracle model errors; preserve original failed evidence and strengthen source-selected seam coverage before the next global run.

periodic_frame.operation: translate each already core-clipped component by an integer number of Web Mercator world widths; retain points, lines, and component shapes
periodic_frame.compactness_guard: Refuse a reference whose framed longitude extent spans half a world or more; do not silently accept geographically extensive records with an ambiguous frame.

dateline_supplement.selection: Original crossing-bbox candidates plus all source bboxes intersecting a 30 Mercator metre strip along either +/-180 degree seam. Select from source geometry bounds, independent of display results.
dateline_supplement.source_bbox_longitude_rule: xmax-xmin > 180 OR xmin <= -180 + margin_degrees OR xmax >= 180 - margin_degrees

native_collapse_classifier.rule: Use the pinned native zoom-32 projection followed by world-coordinate std::round in the pre-simplification no-op check, including half ties away from zero. Later tile-local rounding is distinct and is not used to excuse an absent source ID. Preserve zero-length/source-empty categories and reject any unexplained loss. No length-only exception.

acceptance_controls: Both seam signs and both vertex orders
A source beginning just inside a seam and quantizing to it
Missing real line and remote multipart loss still fail
A genuine central-world chord still fails after component framing
Ambiguous half-world or wider multipart frames fail closed
Native half-tie target plus shorter/longer and phase-shifted surviving/omitted controls
next_gate: Commit corrected verifier and focused tests, then rerun the complete global oracle from a clean checkout. No output geometry or tolerance changes are implied.

supersedes.reason: Source inspection distinguishes the world-coordinate pre-simplification no-op check from later tile-local coordinate rounding. No acceptance threshold or supplemental selection rule changes.
